Before settling on the current [proposal](../phd/index.qmd), I tested the assumptions of an earlier
version on real market data. These eight experiments are kept because their results shaped the current
design. Each states its hypothesis before testing, compares against a benchmark with the same information,
and reports the result whether or not it supports the idea. Two of them are re-tests that overturned my own
earlier findings; those corrections are part of the record.

| Experiment | Question | Finding | Informs |
|---|---|---|---|
| [How backtest selection inflates the Sharpe ratio](backtest-overfitting/index.qmd) | How much does picking the best of many backtests flatter it? | The best of *N* strategies looks good from noise alone; the maximum Sharpe grows like $\sqrt{2\ln N}$. | Counting every trial (09, 10) |
| [Do calendar anomalies survive honest scrutiny?](calendar-anomalies/index.qmd) | Do seasonal effects survive a multiple-testing correction? | None of 29 survive. | A small, fixed indicator set (01) |
| [How far ahead is volatility forecastable?](volatility-forecasting-horizon/index.qmd) | Over what horizon is volatility predictable? | A volatility shock has a half-life of about a month; GARCH and HAR perform similarly. | Volatility and VIX as inputs (01, 02) |
| [Can you monetise forecastable volatility?](volatility-managed-portfolios/index.qmd) | Does forecastable volatility earn excess return? | It buys risk control, not alpha: drawdown roughly halved, no significant excess return. | Risk controls (05) |
| [Does regime-conditioning really sharpen tail probabilities?](h2-calibration-retest/index.qmd) | Re-test of an earlier calibration claim | With a same-information benchmark and Diebold–Mariano tests, 0 of 6 comparisons are significant. My earlier claim did not hold. | Brier scores and forecast tests (02, 10) |
| [Does conditioning on regime actually help?](regime-conditioning-oos/index.qmd) | Does a regime label improve position sizing beyond volatility? | No significant edge over a regime-blind volatility scaler. | Regimes made optional (02) |
| [Is a market-state estimate worth anything?](state-decision-value/index.qmd) | Across 7 assets, does a state estimate add decision value? | It made direction forecasts worse in 53 of 56 pairs and added no risk-adjusted value. | Regimes made optional (02, 08) |
| [Do hard risk limits earn their keep?](h8-risk-limits-retest/index.qmd) | Re-test of an earlier risk-limits claim at equal risk | The cap did nothing, the kill-switch was worse, and a volatility budget was better but not significantly (0 of 9). My earlier claim did not hold. | Deterministic controls (05) |

: Numbers in the last column refer to components of the [system architecture](../phd/architecture.html). {.striped}

## What these results changed

Volatility is forecastable over short horizons, but direction is not, and regime labels added little
beyond volatility itself. That moved the research away from building a better market-state estimator and
towards the decision layer: whether language models reasoning over well-calibrated evidence make better
decisions. The discipline carries over unchanged: same-information benchmarks, proper scoring rules,
Diebold–Mariano tests and a record of every trial.

Code for these experiments is described on the [Code](../code.qmd) page.
